City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
December 5, 2011
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at
05:00 p.m. , on December 5, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on November 30, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Reardon
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Ury
Mayor Leckness
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley
INVOCATION: Council Member Reardon
CLOSED SESSION
Council Member Schlicht asked the City Attorney about the legitimacy of a Closed Session conference for the purpose of discussing the Assistant City Manager’s contract.
Mr. Curley responded that a Closed Session discussion gives the Council the ability to provide staff with negotiation instructions. At the last meeting, staff took the Council’s instruction and created a new draft contract for the Assistant City Manager. During this evening’s closed Session the Council will have the opportunity to review the document before it becomes final and is presented for approval in open session.
All five City Council Members participated in the Closed Session meeting to address item CS1.
CS1.
Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are the City and City's Unrepresented Employee (Assistant City Manager.) The City's Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m., with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council has been considering the scope, nature, and need to enter into an agreement with the incumbent for the Assistant City Manager position. The value in having a contract was to remove any risk that the holder of the position could be self-dealing or have an interest in personnel negotiations. Further, a contract would protect both the City and the employee and provide a clarification of the rights and privileges regarding both employment and separation. Lastly, the contract would give the ability to recognize the position as having some unique nature, both to reward the employee and to manage it in a way that provides the Council with certainty. The City Council has been working diligently, exploring a number of complicated issues and concepts and ultimately, they have authorized a Council subcommittee to work with staff and the employee to come to a mutually beneficial agreement. Mr. Curley requested that the Council remove open session agenda item 20 this evening and reagendaize it at a future date after the Council subcommittee has completed its work.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Recognize the Trabuco Hills High School Boys Cross Country Team for Winning the CIF State Championship
Mayor Leckness presented certificates of recognition to the coaches and members of the Trabuco Hills High School Boys Cross Country Team.
P2.
Neighborhood Watch Presentation
Crime Prevention Specialist Paula Monical presented an overview of the City’s Neighborhood Watch program.
P3.
State of the City Address
Mayor Leckness presented the 2011 State of the City address.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Roy Baker, Orange County Grand Jury, Santa Ana: announced that the Orange County Superior Court Grand Jury is seeking qualified citizens for the 2012-13 Grand Jury. The deadline is January 13, 2012, and applications are available at www.ocgrandjury.org or by calling (714) 834-6747. Beverly Ann Killingback, M.V.: asked the Council to reconsider the City’s request to move a vehicle from her driveway and she stated that she needs it for her disability. Steve Magdziak, M.V.: read excerpts from the Declaration of Independence, the Constitutions of the United States and the State of California, and the Brown Act. He further questioned the Council’s use of closed session meetings to discuss the Assistant City Manager contract.
Christopher Sullivan, M.V.: invited the City Council Members to the Modjeska Playhouse Christmas show on Saturday, December 10, 2011, at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center.
Gail Reavis, M.V.: discussed the notion of rotating the positions of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem and read comments from different Council Members at various times over the years.
Helen Workun, M.V.: complimented Mayor Leckness on his State of the City address and announced that the Mission Viejo history book, The Ageless Land , is available for a donation of $15.00 and she encouraged residents to purchase one as a holiday gift.
Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: offered her condolences to Gail Reavis, discussed the events and programs that are the fabric of our community, and thanked the Mayor for a great State of the City address.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Items 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11, and 12 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Reardon, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Ury, and Mayor Leckness
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes from the Regular City Council Meeting of November 21, 2011, as presented.
6.
Fiber Communication and Traffic Controller Upgrade Project-Various Locations (CIP 797)
(1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.
9.
Annual Measure M-2 Expenditure Report for Fiscal Year Ended 6/30/11
Approved Resolution 11-72 Adopting the Measure M2 Expenditure Report for the City of Mission Viejo.
10.
Fiscal Year 2010-11 Community Development Agency Annual Report
Received, filed and directed staff to transmit the report to the State Controller.
13.
Senior Citizen Transportation Dial-A-Taxi Contract Extension
(1) Approved Amendment No. 5 to the Contract with California Yellow Cab to provide Senior Citizen Transportation Dial-A-Taxi Services through June 30, 2013; and (2) approved contract amounts of $46,000 for fiscal year 2011-2012 and $46,000 for fiscal year 2012-2013 for the services.
14.
Claim Against the City - Morse vs. City of Mission Viejo
Rejected claim.
PUBLIC HEARINGS
OLD BUSINESS
15.
Possible Uses of the Thomas R. Potocki Center
Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.
The following spoke in support of the recommended action: Aileen May, Dana Point; Joy Aldrich, Dana Point; George Katzenberger, Irvine; Scott Ramirez, Outta Bounds, Rancho Santa Margarita; and Christopher Sullivan, Modjeska Playhouse, M.V.
Motion made by , seconded by , to
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Reardon, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Ury, and Mayor Leckness
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
NEW BUSINESS
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
7.
Rancho Mission Viejo Consolidation of Fee Obligations Funding Agreement
Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.
Council Member Schlicht asked questions of staff.
Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: stated that the Rancho Mission Viejo Company has always been a partner with the City of Mission Viejo so she wholeheartedly supports the recommended action.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to approve the "Consolidation of Fee Obligations for Planned Communities" Funding Agreement between Rancho Mission Viejo and the City of Mission Viejo.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Reardon, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Ury, and Mayor Leckness
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
RECESS
At the hour of 8:21 p.m., Mayor Leckness declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:33 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (Continued)
3.
Check Register Dated November 11, 2011 in the Amount of $327,240.15
Council Member Schlicht inquired about Dell computer purchases listed on page 19 of this item and on page 37 of item 4.
City Manager Wilberg responded that he would check into the computer purchases and get back to the City Council with a response.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to ratifiy the accompanying check register.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Reardon, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Ury, and Mayor Leckness
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
4.
Check Register Dated November 18, 2011 in the Amount of $2,515,800.52
Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment made to Animal Pest Management for a coyote trap and she expressed concern with the practice. She asked staff if trapping coyotes would increase the rabbit population. Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay replied that the City recently trapped a coyote that had been frequently seen near a school. He noted that he would verify the location with staff and get back to the Council with a more detailed explanation.
Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to ratify the accompanying check register.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Reardon, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Ury, and Mayor Leckness
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
5.
Cooperative Agreements with the Orange County Transportation Authority for the Crown Valley Parkway and Marguerite Parkway Traffic Signal Synchronization Programs (Project P)
Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with the City’s light synchronization programs and stated that she has noticed that cross traffic now sits longer at red lights. She asked if there has been a noticeable increase in traffic accidents.
Council Member Kelley stated that many residents would say that their number one concern is traffic and congestion. She feels that the City has done a wonderful job alleviating traffic with these signal synchronization efforts.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1) approve Cooperative Agreement No. C-1-3001 with the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) for the Crown Valley Parkway Traffic Signal Synchronization Program (Project P); and (2) approve Cooperative Agreement No. C-1-3020 with the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) for the Marguerite Parkway Traffic Signal Synchronization Program (Project P).
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Reardon, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Ury, and Mayor Leckness
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
8.
Funding Provided by a New Statewide Franchise for the Purchase or Upgrade of Mission Viejo Television (MVTV) Capital Equipment
Council Member Schlicht asked if the 1% franchise fee covers the entire cost of the MVTV operations and whether or not staff can explore broadcasting the Planning and Transportation Commission Meetings.
By consensus, the City Council directed staff to look into the potential broadcasting of the Planning and Transportation Commission Meetings.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to adopt Resolution No. 11-71 Amending the Fiscal Year 2011-2012 Budget for Costs Related to the Purchase of Mission Viejo Television Capital Equipment.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Reardon, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Ury, and Mayor Leckness
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
11.
Community Services Funding Program - Funding for Fiscal Year 2011-2012
Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report. Council Member Schlicht discussed the recommendation to give donations to Timeless Melodies and Modjeska playhouse. She stated that she is concerned that there is a conflict of interest and a manipulation and exploitation of the process. She believes that if there is an appearance of a conflict of interest, there is a conflict of interest.
Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to bifurcate the item and vote on Cultural Arts categories C and G separately.

12.
Approve Agreement with OCTA for the Transportation Enhancement project grant on Marguerite Parkway from Via Florecer to Estanciero
Council Member Schlicht asked how many acres of landscape will be rehabilitated with this program. Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay estimated that it is a little under a mile. Council Member Schlicht stated that the City is wasting money on projects like this and is spending its wealth away.
The City Council Members inquired about the use of these grant funds and Mr. Rattay described the criteria for the grant and stated that the intent is to create an enhanced driving experience and to do something above and beyond general landscaping.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, Approved agreement number C-1-2629 with OCTA for the Marguerite Parkway Median Island Civic Core Enhancement project through OCTA Transportation Enhancement Act and authorize the Mayor to sign the agreement.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

Council Member Kelley, Council Member Reardon, Mayor Pro Tem Ury, and Mayor Leckness

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
16.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Council Member Kelley stated that there has not been a recent meeting of the Orange County Fire Authority Board of Directors however she provided a few OCFA updates.
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: asked the Council to assist him in finding out where three firefighters were on OCFA open house day and stated that he is having trouble finding out how a City can reduce OCFA contract costs.
17.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Ury presented the report.
18.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Leckness announced that he had nothing to report.
19.
SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
City Manager Wilberg drew the Council’s attention to a summary update memo on the AARP senior citizen tax assistance program at the Community Center. The City has satisfied all of the technical and logistical problems however the AARP district coordinator has not found someone to provide the service. Staff will continue to pursue other options and he noted that tax service is available at Saddleback Church. Mr. Wilberg further noted that he has provided another memo with an update on the Marguerite Tennis Center improvement project.
Council Member Schlicht inquired about the City’s surplus computers and whether or not they will be offered for sale to the public.
Mr. Wilberg noted that staff intends to wholesale the surplus equipment this year.
City Attorney’s Report
City Attorney Curley reminded the Council that agenda item 20 was removed from the Agenda.
20.
Employment Contract for Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, W. Keith Rattay
This item was not considered.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
21.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley commented on agenda item 13. She stated that the Dial-A-Taxi program for seniors provides service 7 days a week, 24 hours a day, within Mission Viejo and some nearby locations. Participants must be 80 years of age or older, 65 or older if disabled, 60 years or older with a revoked license, or unable to drive. Each one-way trip is $15.00 with the participant paying $5.00 and the City paying the $10.00 portion. Council Member Kelley noted that Mission Viejo has proven to be a leader and the City of Laguna Hills is now replicating our system. She commended staff members Leslie McDonald and Kelly Doyle and Mayor Pro Tem Ury for their work on the Dial-A-Taxi program. Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at various recent events including Santa’s arrival and she reminded residents that Santa will be in his workshop every Wednesday, Saturday, and Sunday evening from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. She also discussed her attendance at brunch with Santa and she commended the Saddleback Unified School District Recreation Department for this event. Lastly, Santa visited Mission Viejo on the Metrolink train and Council Member Kelley asked staff why this event was not offered to residents last year.
City Manager Wilberg announced that cost was a factor. The City appealed to Metrolink and the fee to stop at the Mission Viejo/Laguna Niguel station was underwritten by several consulting firms, making the event possible again this year. Council Member Kelley extended her condolences to Gail Reavis on the loss of her husband and she concluded her comments by announcing that the Community of Character word for the month of December is caring.
Council Member Reardon
Council Member Reardon outlined her attendance at recent events including the grand opening of the South County Auto Collision Center which is affiliated with Lexus. She also attended the grand re-opening of McDonalds and she encouraged residents to visit the restaurant to see the historical pictures on display. She stated that the owners are great people and they opened the first Ronald McDonald house when their daughter was diagnosed with leukemia. Council Member Reardon thanked her colleagues for their support on the anniversary of her first year on the City Council. She also thanked staff and each of the department directors. She stated that she looks forward to another great year ahead and to learning more. Finally, Council Member Reardon wished everyone a Merry Christmas and happy Hanukkah and she encouraged those who celebrate Christmas to remember the reason for the season.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht wished everyone a Merry Christmas, happy Hanukkah, and happy holidays. She expressed her wish for a prosperous New Year, a better economy, and she encouraged everyone to remember those who are less fortunate. Council Member Schlicht expressed her thanks to the Mission Viejo High School Diablos football team for giving their fans a great season. She reminded residents that 2,403 Americans lost their lives at Pearl Harbor 70 years ago today, in what was the beginning of a long war fighting for our freedoms. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments by stating that she will forever be grateful for getting to know a man named Rick (Reavis.) A man who never compromised his values and who always had a smile on his face.
Mayor Pro Tem Ury
Mayor Pro Tem Ury stated that he is glad that Council Member Kelley commented on the Dial-A-Taxi program. Leslie McDonald has done a phenomenal job with the program but the inception of the idea was Council Member Kelley’s and he is glad the program is doing well. Mayor Pro Tem Ury stated that he too had a fun time at the re-opening of the McDonalds and the owner and his team did a fantastic job. He also attended the Santa’s Arrival event and he noted that it wouldn’t be possible without the Mission Viejo Activities Committee. He wished everyone a Merry Christmas, happy Hanukkah, happy New Year and a safe holiday season.
Mayor Leckness
Mayor Leckness announced that he sat in on a focus group with the American Cancer Society where he learned a lot about the organization’s history and accomplishments. Next June voters will decide if $1 per pack of cigarettes sold will be designated for cancer research. Mayor Leckness concluded his comments by wishing residents and his colleagues a Merry Christmas and Happy Hanukkah.
CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION
22.
Election of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem
City Clerk Karen Hamman called for nominations for Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem for 2012.
Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, to elect Dave Leckness as Mayor for the year 2012. The motion died for lack of a second.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to elect Frank Ury as Mayor for the year 2012.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Reardon, Mayor Pro Tem Ury, and Mayor Leckness
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
None
Motion made by Council Member Reardon, to elect Cathy Schlicht as Mayor Pro Tem for the year 2012. The motion died for lack of a second.
Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to elect Rhonda Reardon as Mayor Pro Tem for the year 2012.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Reardon, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Ury, and Mayor Leckness
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 9:50 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting in memory of Richard Dixon and Rick Reavis, to Tuesday, January 3, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
